bullets.text: A crowd crush occurred in the front standing area at the Thornlea Park festival ground in Verrow on the evening of July 25, 2025.
Eleven people died, nine at the scene and two in hospital, and 54 people were treated in total.
The event was suspended and attendees were evacuated through the north gates; a major incident was declared by police, ambulance and hospital services.
A criminal investigation into crowd management was opened and the venue's large-event licences were suspended pending review.
Attendees at the front of the main stage report being crushed and unable to move during the headline set.
The performance is stopped and people are lifted out over the front barrier.
Eyewitnesses report multiple unconscious casualties and resuscitation attempts on the ground.
The festival announces the event is suspended and directs attendees to leave through the north gates.
The ambulance service responds to a declared major incident with multiple casualties reported.
Police confirm a major incident at the festival ground and the city infirmary declares a major incident.
Police state there was no structural collapse and that the incident was a crowd crush.
The ambulance service reports 8 confirmed dead at the scene and 42 taken to hospital.
Police state there is no evidence of any weapon, addressing a circulating rumour.
The death toll is given as 11, with nine deaths at the scene and two in hospital, and 54 people treated.
A criminal investigation into crowd management is announced and the council begins a licensing review.
All 11 deaths are formally identified, a public vigil is held at the venue gates, and large-event licences are suspended.
Eight deaths were confirmed at the scene in the first official casualty statement.
The death toll was subsequently given as 11, comprising nine deaths at the scene and two in hospital.
All 11 deaths were formally identified and families informed before names were released.
Reports of 30 deaths circulated in two outlets against the confirmed figure of 11.
Forty-two people were taken to hospital in the first phase of the response.
Fifty-four people were treated in total across the response.
Eyewitnesses reported multiple unconscious casualties carried from the front standing area.
Nineteen patients were admitted, four of them in critical condition.
Twelve patients were discharged, with two remaining in critical condition at that point.
The city infirmary declared a major incident and asked the public to attend only for emergencies.
The festival was suspended and attendees were evacuated through the north gates.
The city council suspended all large-event licences at Thornlea Park pending its review.
Police stated there was no structural collapse at the venue, contrary to circulating reports.
Attendees were directed to leave the festival ground through the north gates after the event was suspended.
Casualties were lifted out over the front barrier by other attendees and stewards.
The incident was assessed as a crowd crush in the front standing area rather than a structural failure.
Eyewitnesses described a surge from behind approximately twenty minutes into the headline set.
Survivors described barriers that funnelled the crowd toward a narrowing area at the front.
Police stated there was no evidence of any weapon at the venue.
The ambulance service responded to a declared major incident with multiple units at the venue.
Police declared a major incident at the festival ground and coordinated the scene response.
Two hospitals received casualties, with the city infirmary declaring a major incident.
Police established a casualty bureau with a published number for families seeking information.
Police opened a criminal investigation into crowd management at the event.
Attendees publicly urged others near the main stage to move back and stop pushing forward.
The city infirmary asked the public to attend only for emergencies during the major incident.
The ambulance service and police issued sequential casualty figures during the response.
Police corrected a circulating claim that the stage had collapsed, stating the incident was a crowd crush.
Police corrected a circulating claim that a weapon had caused the surge, stating the rumour was unfounded.
Police corrected reporting of 30 deaths against the confirmed figure of 11.
Relatives publicly appealed for information about attendees in the front standing area.
A hospital issued a blood donation appeal while receiving casualties.
The Verrow Community Trust opened a support centre at the civic hall for families and festivalgoers.
Volunteers provided counselling, refreshments and space at the civic hall from the night of the incident.
Residents responded to the blood donation appeal in numbers, with queues reported at the donation centre.
Police and the ambulance service held a joint briefing on the response and the ongoing investigation.
A decision was taken to suspend all large-event licences at the venue pending the licensing review.
The city council opened a review of the licensing conditions for events at Thornlea Park.
The promoter stated the event had been staffed to the levels required by the licence.
Volunteers staffed the civic hall support centre continuously from the night of the incident.
A public vigil was held at the venue gates, attended by thousands, with flowers left along the fence line.
Eyewitness accounts conveyed distress and disbelief at conditions in the front standing area.
Public frustration was directed at circulating rumours about a stage collapse and a weapon.
Public solidarity was expressed through the blood donation response and the vigil.
